title: Lowering the Barrier to AI-Driven Inspection: A No-Code Workflow for Automated Structural Defect Detection
abstract: arXiv:2608.25176v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) is essential in modern engineering, providing data for condition-based maintenance, lifecycle assessment, and predictive decision-making. Traditionally, SHM relied on visual inspection to detect defects such as cracks and deformations. Early computer vision (CV) methods, including thresholding, edge detection, and handcrafted features, aimed to automate this process but were highly sensitive to noise, imaging variations, and multiscale defects, limiting their reliability. translated_title: 降低AI驱动检测的门槛：自动化结构缺陷检测的无代码工作流
translated_abstract: 结构健康监测（SHM）在现代工程中至关重要，为基于状态的维护、生命周期评估和预测性决策提供数据。传统上，SHM依赖目视检查来检测裂缝和变形等缺陷。早期的计算机视觉（CV）方法，包括阈值分割、边缘检测和手工特征，旨在自动化这一过程，但对噪声、成像变化和多尺度缺陷高度敏感，限制了其可靠性。近年来，机器学习的最新进展，特别是卷积神经网络（CNN）和You Only Look Once（YOLO），提高了缺陷检测的准确性并实现了实时分析。然而，由于数据标注、模型训练和部署等技术障碍（通常需要编程专业知识），SHM中的采用仍然有限。为解决这一差距，我们引入了YOLOEZ，一个开源的、基于图形用户界面（GUI）的工具。
tldr: 本文提出了YOLOEZ，一个开源无代码图形界面工具，旨在消除编程障碍，使非专家也能轻松进行AI驱动的结构缺陷检测。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces YOLOEZ, an open-source no-code GUI tool designed to remove programming barriers, enabling non-experts to easily perform AI-driven structural defect detection.
